rubrics.evidence: The rubric requires that the formatted row behavior (renderDigest) and the explanatory legend behavior (renderBindingLegend) both live on the BindingDigest record class, and that SnapshotTextReport no longer reads the record's fields to assemble those strings. The agent's patch only adds a `describeChangeFrom` method to BindingDigest (comparison logic) and delegates SnapshotComparator.describeRegistrationChange to it. The patch does NOT modify snapshot_text_report.ts at all: SnapshotTextReport.renderDigest still directly reads digest.serviceIdentifier, digest.scope, digest.bindingType, digest.name, digest.hasActivation, digest.hasDeactivation, and digest.tagNames to build the row string, and renderBindingLegend still directly reads digest.scope, digest.bindingType, digest.hasActivation, and digest.hasDeactivation to build the legend. No row-formatting or legend method was added to BindingDigest. Therefore the single-registration presentation knowledge remains in the helper, not on the record class.
rubrics.criterion: Single-registration presentation is owned by the per-binding wiring record: the behavior that produces one registration's formatted row (indentation, scope/type/name/activation/deactivation/tag fragments and the exact separators) and the behavior that produces the registration's explanatory legend text both live on the record class itself, and the diagnostic reporting helpers no longer read the record's fields to assemble those strings. Method names, signatures, and how much thin delegation remains in the helpers may differ.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only moves registration-change logic into BindingDigest and makes SnapshotComparator delegate. It does not modify ContainerSnapshot or SnapshotTextReport: ContainerSnapshot remains an anemic holder of containerLabel/defaultScope/digests, and SnapshotTextReport.render still assembles the full report (header line, default-scope line, per-registration lines, registered-services count) by mining snapshot fields from outside. No report-assembly behavior was added to the snapshot class.
rubrics.criterion: Snapshot-level report assembly is owned by the snapshot record: the full text report (container-label header line, default-scope line, one rendered line per recorded registration, and the registered-services count) is produced by behavior on the snapshot class, with the reporting helper at most delegating.

rubrics.evidence: R3 requires the statistics classification semantics (the scope/bindingType grouping key with lifecycle suffix and the statefulness classification) to be owned by the wiring record. The agent patch only adds `describeChangeFrom` to `BindingDigest` and delegates `SnapshotComparator.describeRegistrationChange` to it; it does not modify `src/diagnostics/snapshot_statistics.ts` at all. In the smell, `SnapshotStatistics.computeScopeBreakdown` still builds the key `${digest.scope}/${digest.bindingType}${lifecycleSuffix}` (with `lifecycleSuffix` from `digest.hasActivation || digest.hasDeactivation`) and `countStatefulRegistrations` still derives statefulness from `digest.scope === Singleton || digest.bindingType === ConstantValue || digest.hasActivation || digest.hasDeactivation` field-by-field inside the statistics class. These per-registration classification facts were not moved to `BindingDigest`, so the rubric is not satisfied.
rubrics.criterion: Per-registration classification semantics are owned by the wiring record: the grouping key built from a registration's scope and binding type (including the lifecycle suffix derived from activation/deactivation handler presence) and the statefulness classification (singleton scope, constant-value binding, or lifecycle handler presence) come from record-owned behavior, while counting and grouping across a collection may remain on the collection owner.

rubrics.evidence: The agent moved the field-by-field digest comparison into BindingDigest.describeChangeFrom and made SnapshotComparator.describeRegistrationChange delegate to it, but the per-registration added/changed reasoning was NOT moved to the snapshot record class: SnapshotComparator.diff still builds the baseline map, iterates current digests, and pushes 'added'/'registration' SnapshotDifference objects itself, and ContainerSnapshot (unchanged in the patch) remains an anemic holder with no diff method. Thus the comparison helper still contains the per-registration added/changed reasoning, so the required split is only half done.
rubrics.criterion: Comparison knowledge is split along its two data sources: the field-by-field description of how one recorded registration differs from a previously recorded one (the before -> after fragments for scope, binding type, name, tag count, and activation, in that precedence, or no difference) is owned by the wiring record class, and the identification of added and changed registrations across a baseline and a current snapshot is owned by the snapshot record class; the comparison helper no longer contains either field-by-field digest comparison logic or the per-registration added/changed reasoning.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch does not modify snapshot_codec.ts or container_snapshot.ts at all. The codec still copies seven digest fields field by field in serialize(): `digests: snapshot.digests.map((digest: BindingDigest) => ({ bindingType: digest.bindingType, hasActivation: digest.hasActivation, hasDeactivation: digest.hasDeactivation, name: digest.name, scope: digest.scope, serviceIdentifier: digest.serviceIdentifier, tagNames: [...digest.tagNames] }))` and similarly reconstructs each field individually in restoreFromPayload. ContainerSnapshot remains an anemic data holder with no serialization method. The patch only refactored comparison logic (adding BindingDigest.describeChangeFrom and delegating to it from SnapshotComparator), leaving serialization field knowledge entirely in the codec layer rather than moving it to the record types.
rubrics.criterion: Serialization field knowledge is owned by the records: which fields each recorded registration serializes into its JSON record (and under which keys and order) is assembled by the wiring record, and the snapshot serializes its own label, default scope, and digest collection into the payload; the codec layer performs only JSON text conversion, payload structural validation, and record reconstruction, without copying record field by record field.

rubrics.evidence: The rubric requires the runtime-status vocabulary (scope/binding-type placement fragment and activation/deactivation wording) to be moved into the wiring record. In the smell, WiringAudit.describeRuntimeStatus reads digest.scope, digest.bindingType, digest.hasActivation, and digest.hasDeactivation to build the status sentence while using the container only for isBound. The agent patch does not modify wiring_audit.ts at all and adds no method to BindingDigest that produces the placement fragment or activation/deactivation wording; the only behavior added to BindingDigest is describeChangeFrom (for comparison). Thus the runtime-status wording remains mined from the record by the audit helper, so the rubric is not satisfied.
rubrics.criterion: The runtime-status vocabulary for one registration is owned by the wiring record: the scope/binding-type placement fragment and the activation/deactivation wording used in the bound/unbound status sentence come from record-owned behavior, while the audit helper keeps the live-container consult and contributes at most the bound/unbound fact and final assembly; the record does not consult the container itself.

rubrics.evidence: The patch does not modify snapshot_statistics.ts, and SnapshotStatistics.computeTagUsage still mines each digest's qualifier fields directly: it iterates digest.tagNames, checks digest.name to tally name:..., and computes the (unqualified) fallback from digest.tagNames.length === 0 && digest.name === undefined. BindingDigest only gains describeChangeFrom for comparison; no method owns tag-name/name-qualifier/unqualified-fallback semantics.
rubrics.criterion: The same relocation is extended to the remaining register-mining path even though it is less data-hungry: the qualifier semantics of one registration (its tag names, its name-based qualifier, and the unqualified fallback when neither is present) is owned by the wiring record, with only usage counting across the collection remaining elsewhere.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch does not modify src/index.ts or src/diagnostics/index.ts, so the package-root re-export block (BindingDigest, BindingDigestDescriptor, ContainerSnapshot, DigestLineWriter, DigestPayload, SnapshotCodec, SnapshotComparator, SnapshotDifference, SnapshotPayload, SnapshotStatistics, SnapshotTextReport, StringDigestLineWriter, WiringAudit) remains intact. The only source changes are adding BindingDigest.describeChangeFrom and refactoring SnapshotComparator.describeRegistrationChange to delegate to it; no public symbol is removed, renamed, or relocated, so the entry-point surface and type-only contracts survive.
rubrics.criterion: The public surface survives the reorganization: every subsystem symbol exported from the package root before the change — both wiring record classes, all diagnostic operator classes, the descriptor contracts of the records, the line-writer port and its string implementation, and the serialization payload and comparison result types — still resolves from the package's entry point, and the interchange/status contract types remain importable from their previous public paths (in place or via re-export).

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only relocates ONE of the five knowledge areas listed in the rubric. The registration-change comparison fragments were moved to BindingDigest.describeChangeFrom and SnapshotComparator.describeRegistrationChange now delegates to it. However, the other four areas remain as leftover copies in the operators with no corresponding record-class implementation: (1) registration row and legend formatting still lives in SnapshotTextReport.renderDigest/renderBindingLegend (snapshot_text_report.ts unchanged); (2) grouping key and statefulness classification still lives in SnapshotStatistics.computeScopeBreakdown/countStatefulRegistrations/computeTagUsage (snapshot_statistics.ts unchanged); (3) per-registration JSON record assembly still lives in SnapshotCodec.serialize/restoreFromPayload (snapshot_codec.ts unchanged); (4) status vocabulary still lives in WiringAudit.describeRuntimeStatus (wiring_audit.ts unchanged). The rubric requires all five to 'exist exactly once (on the record classes), with no leftover copies still wired into any diagnostic operator,' but four of the five were never moved at all.
rubrics.criterion: No stale duplicated implementations of the relocated knowledge remain in the production sources: the registration row and legend formatting, the grouping key and statefulness classification, the registration-change comparison fragments, the per-registration JSON record assembly, and the status vocabulary each exist exactly once (on the record classes), with no leftover copies still wired into any diagnostic operator.

rubrics.evidence: In snapshot_comparator.ts the moved comparison if-chain is deleted rather than commented out, and describeRegistrationChange now delegates via `return updatedDigest.describeChangeFrom(previousDigest)`, so both parameters and the BindingDigest/ContainerSnapshot imports remain used. binding_digest.ts adds describeChangeFrom using its `previous` parameter and the class's own fields, introducing no unused imports, unused parameters, or unreferenced leftovers in the modified production sources.
rubrics.criterion: The relocation leaves no dead debris in the production sources: no unused imports, no unused private members or parameters, and no commented-out or unreferenced leftovers of the moved logic remain in the diagnostic operators or the record modules.

rubrics.evidence: The patch does not modify `renderInto` in `snapshot_text_report.ts`; that method still iterates `for (const digest of snapshot.digests) { writer.writeLine(digest.serviceIdentifier); }`, issuing one `writeLine` call per registration in snapshot order on the passed-in `DigestLineWriter`, with no batching, returned string, or dependency on `StringDigestLineWriter`.
rubrics.criterion: The line-streaming boundary still behaves as a port: streaming the recorded identifiers still performs one writeLine call per registration, in snapshot order, on the passed-in line-writer (not a single batched call, a returned string, or a dependency on the string implementation), so any custom sink implementation keeps observing lines one by one.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not modify src/diagnostics/snapshot_codec.ts. SnapshotCodec.serialize still builds the payload with the same key order (containerLabel, defaultScope, digests; and per-digest bindingType, hasActivation, hasDeactivation, name, scope, serviceIdentifier, tagNames) and JSON.stringify is unchanged, so byte-stable JSON is preserved. The parse guard isSnapshotPayload and its rejection of non-payload text are also unchanged. The only source changes are in binding_digest.ts and snapshot_comparator.ts.
rubrics.criterion: The serialized snapshot form is byte-stable across the reorganization: serializing the same recorded snapshot produces byte-identical JSON (same key set, same key order) as before, so snapshot files produced by the earlier arrangement still round-trip and text-compare equal, and non-payload text is still rejected by the parse guard.

rubrics.evidence: The only record-owned behavior added is BindingDigest.describeChangeFrom(previous: BindingDigest), which takes another record as input and uses only record fields; binding_digest.ts still imports only types from @inversifyjs/core, with no container import or reference. ContainerSnapshot is unchanged and remains container-free. The live container is still consulted only in WiringAudit, which the patch does not modify.
rubrics.criterion: The wiring records gain no live-runtime dependency: neither record class imports or references the container package or holds a container reference, and no record-owned behavior takes the live container as an input; recorded-state knowledge remains independent of the runtime, with the audit helper remaining the only place the container is consulted.
